analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date on line 3 and adds an 'Add-On Hold' test section after the Provider Endpoint Resumption And Logout section, around head lines 767-790. I examined both base units, covering lines 1-474 and 475-945, plus the patch excerpt. The excerpt is truncated mid-sentence ('The peer check is exercised only neg...'), so the tail of the new section was not visible.

The new section describes test suites for an add-on hold feature: AddonIPC, an AF_UNIX socket, flock, peer policy, a draining heartbeat, ProviderBusyWire and register encodings. It says the tests need no weights or credentials and use a private temporary runtime directory. This is documentation only. It adds no runtime code, no new endpoint, and no change to the key, attestation or authorization paths.

The following are not verifiable from the supplied evidence:
- The add-on hold feature itself. If it ships in the same PR, its local IPC (the peer-credential policy, socket permissions and the hold-record store) would touch TB-003 and TB-002. It could affect T-053-style stale authorization, because the hold interacts with draining and reconnect, and T-010 and T-046-style availability concerns.
- Whether the hold can be set by an untrusted local process. The documented peer policy refuses the test process and the socket is owner-only, which suggests intent to restrict it. That is the control to review in the source units of this PR, which are not in this batch.

The canonical threat model has no entry for the add-on hold IPC surface. A later pass should consider whether TB-003 or TB-002 need updating once the source changes are visible. The existing T-041 context is unaffected by this doc edit. No finding is raised against documentation text.
